candidates.source_claim: For a right R-module M and an (R,T)-bimodule N, the formula (m⊗n)t=m⊗(nt) induces a right T-action on M⊗_R N. For an (S,R)-bimodule M and a left R-module N, s(m⊗n)=(sm)⊗n induces a left S-action. With both actions on the same factors, they commute and make M⊗_R N an (S,T)-bimodule.
candidates.diagram_kind: balanced tensor product with commuting outer S and T actions
candidates.why_warranted: A small action diagram can make the common middle algebra R, the two outer algebras S and T, and the direction of each action visible. This is an optional communication aid; no proof needs a diagram.
concrete_content_to_draw_or_check: Use one shared pair of factors: _S M_R and _R N_T, with codomain M⊗_R N. Label the left S action on M and the right T action on N.
On elementary tensors show s·(m⊗n)=(sm)⊗n and (m⊗n)·t=m⊗(nt), for s∈S, t∈T.
Show the balancing relation (mr)⊗n=m⊗(rn) is preserved by both actions; for the right action use (mr)⊗(nt)=m⊗r(nt)=m⊗(rn)t, and for the left action use (s(mr))⊗n=(sm)⊗(rn).
Show the commuting square on elementary tensors: s·((m⊗n)·t)=(sm)⊗(nt)=(s·(m⊗n))·t.
correctness_checks: The right-action construction needs M right R and N an (R,T)-bimodule; its action map is on M⊗_R N and is right T, not left T.
The left-action construction needs M an (S,R)-bimodule and N left R; its action map is on M⊗_R N and is left S.
For the combined (S,T)-bimodule claim, both actions must be on the same M and N: _S M_R and _R N_T. Keep the left and right outer algebras distinct in the notation.
Check balancing via the commuting factor actions before using the universal property; then check module laws and commutation on elementary tensors, extending by additivity and generation.

The screenshot proof step 4.1 cites the earlier separate constructions. The diagram should identify the common M,N instance required for the combined claim; otherwise the cited separate instances may be mistaken for actions on different tensor products.
candidates.why_not_confirmed: No diagram is present to assess for mathematical errors. A diagram is optional rather than required for the elementary construction. The common-factor hypotheses for the combined claim are only called the 'evident handed situation', and the proof's separate M,N and M′,N′ descriptions make a diagram useful for disambiguation; the standard shared-factor formulation verifies directly.
